items.title: Strategy's Bitcoin Buying Spree Signals Market Shift
points: Strategy bought 4,603 BTC for $370M at average price of $80,318 per coin, its first purchase since June after a three-month buying pause.
The firm paid 29% more per coin than what it sold for during May-August ($62,250), having sold 6,948 BTC for total ~$432M losses on timing.
Strategy now holds 845,050 BTC, still slightly below its peak of 847,363 BTC reached before summer selling began.

Tom Lee's Bitmine acquired $131 million of Ethereum (53,501 ETH), its largest purchase since June, suggesting coordinated institutional re-entry into markets by digital asset treasury firms (companies that hold crypto assets on their balance sheets).

items.title: Cronos Network Halted After $75M Tectonic Protocol Exploit
points: An attacker drained $75M from the Tectonic lending protocol (a service that lets users borrow and lend crypto assets) on Crypto.com's Cronos blockchain through an unspecified vulnerability.
Validators froze the entire Cronos network to prevent further damage; $6M had already been bridged to Ethereum before the halt.
Remaining ~$69M in stolen funds are currently stranded on the halted Cronos network, unable to move or be recovered without a chain restart.
This highlights a critical failure point where halting the blockchain prevents both attacker escapes and legitimate transaction processing.

items.title: Ancient Bitcoin Holdings Waking Up in 2026
points: Bitcoin holdings untouched for 10+ years are moving at unusually high rates in 2026, potentially indicating long-term holders exiting positions.

items.title: Ex-White House Teleprompter Operator Fined for Prediction Market Insider Trading
points: A former White House teleprompter operator settled a $172K fine for trading on prediction markets (platforms where users bet on the outcome of real-world events) using advance knowledge of presidential speeches.
This marks the first insider trading case in political information markets.
